question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is **"since."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We use **"since"** with a point in time in the past.
 
• It is often used with the present perfect tense to show that the reason or cause is still relevant.
 
 
• **Example**: *I haven't seen her **since__** she moved to London.*
 
 
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
• **Correct passage*****:***

Dill ate, and ate and ate. He hadn’t eaten __**since**__ last night. He used all his money for a ticket, ______ (2) ______the train, as he had done many times, coolly chatted with the conductor, to ______ (3) ______ Dill was a familiar sight, but he had not the nerve to invoke the rule on small children travelling a distance alone; if you’ve lost your money the conductor will ______ (4) ______ you enough for dinner and your father will ______ (5) ______ him back at the end of the line. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Because"** is also used to introduce a reason or cause, but it is not as formal as "since.".
 
• **"About"** is not appropriate in this context as it does not relate to a reason or cause.
 
• **"For"** can be used to indicate a reason or purpose, but it is not as common as "since."
